pages.title: About – Catalyst Bible College
content: Where everyone majors in changing the world.
Catalyst Bible College is powered by Nelson University.
With meager beginnings in 1928, brave men and women of God overcame relentless spiritual attacks and built Visalia First on prayer and the presence of God.

Our world is changing at lightning speed, but there is one thing that has not changed: the power of the Gospel and a Spirit-filled church. In every adult service for the past 27 years, someone has accepted Jesus as their Savior and committed their life to Him. With multiple ministries and services happening throughout the week, lives are consistently being changed for the Kingdom!

Students of Catalyst Bible College have the incredible opportunity to work alongside strong ministry leaders at Visalia First as they develop leadership skills, a strong network of peers, and a deep knowledge of the Bible.
Located strategically in the Central Valley of California, Visalia First is under an hour away from the Sequoia National Park, three hours away from Los Angeles, and two hours to the nearest beach.
Our campus is in the perfect location to have hands-on ministry experience across our partner churches.

Visalia First and Catalyst Bible College are committed to produce credentialed, high-functioning ministers for the Assemblies of God with little to no debt. This is why we are offering more than $100,000 worth of scholarships for students to apply for each year. The average CBC student will graduate receiving close to $10,000 in scholarship dollars.
Contact us for more information on how to apply for scholarships and become a CBC scholar.

pages.title: Why CBC? – Catalyst Bible College
content: This chart shows top Christian universities and their cost of tuition. The prices do not reflect the additional costs of housing, meal plans, and general fees that each student is required to pay.

Through our partnership with Nelson University, students are able to apply for Federal Financial Aid. and offers a variety of scholarship opportunities for students. Price comparisons below represent actual private Christian Institutions with similar degree programs.
Chart data (from saved page copy): School 1 $142,140 · School 2 $121,728 · School 3 $108,560 · School 4 $103,688 · School 5 $163,200 · Catalyst Bible College $36,600 (Total Tuition Cost each).
Annual Tuition $7,320 ($305/credit hour, 24 hours per year)
Annual Site Fee $4,000 ($2,000 in the Fall and $2,000 in the Spring)
Graduation Fee $150 One time fee to be paid the semester of graduation

We want all of our students to be well-versed in all aspects of ministry and Practicums are one way we are able to do this! Each student will rotate through Catalyst Bible College's three different Practicum focuses. These areas have been carefully curated to emphasize key elements of ministry and leadership development.

Practicums are required for Church Leadership majors, but can also be utilized as a resource for our other offered degree programs. Each student not in the Church Leadership program is highly encouraged to participate in Practicums.

One of the goals of CBC is for every student to graduate with a passion and heart for missions. That is why we have developed the Catalyst World Experience. Every eligible student will have the opportunity to visit five foreign countries during their four years with Catalyst. These experiences come at no additional cost to the student through generous partners and donations. We aim to visit South America, Europe, Africa, Asia and the Holy Land all before a student graduates our program.
To learn more about the Catalyst World Experience, set up a meeting with our Admissions Office.

pages.title: Programs – Catalyst Bible College
content: Catalyst Bible College is powered by Nelson University.
Visalia First offers Catalyst Bible College as a Partner Site in partnership with Nelson University. All graduating students will receive a diploma from Nelson University. www.nelson.edu

Nelson University (formerly Southwestern Assemblies of God University) is named in honor of founder PC Nelson. The University's vision of being a distinguished Christian university that equips Spirit-empowered leaders with career and ministry skills by providing affordable education, hands-on training opportunities, and innovative academic programs remains unchanged. Nelson University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associates, baccalaureate, master's and doctorate degrees. Degree-granting institutions also may offer credentials such as certificates and diplomas at approved degree levels. Questions about the accreditation of Nelson University may be directed in writing to the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges at 1866 Southern Lane, Decatur, Georgia 30033-4097, by calling 404-679-4500, or by using information available on SACSCOC's website www.sacscoc.org. For more information on Nelson's accreditation, you can also visit: www.nelson.edu/about/accreditation

Through Nelson University, Catalyst Bible College is able to offer six different undergraduate degree programs, as well as a variety of graduate degrees. Regardless of the degree a student chooses to pursue, every student will have the opportunity to take part in our "Lifestyle of Learning" initiative. Students will be invited to conferences and special lectures that create an atmosphere for them to collaborate, grow, and develop in their callings.
Click on the icon beside each program to learn more about it.
The B.A. in Church Leadership will equip students for modern partical [sic] ministry. Students will choose 24 hours of specialization in their degree. This is an on-campus only program.
General Education Units: 57 · Major Units: 45 · Elective Units: 18 · Total Program Units: 120

The B.A. in Humanitarian Relief and Development is a degree plan built in partnership with world humanitarian leader Convoy of Hope, emphasizing compassion-based initiatives, poverty alleviation, and transformational community development. This is an on-campus only program.
General Education Units: 57 · Major Units: 45 · Elective Units: 18 · Total Program Units: 120
The B.A. program provides students with a solid business foundation. Students can choose to minor in accounting, business administration, or marketing.
General Education Units: 51 · Major Units: 39 · Elective Units: 30 · Total Program Units: 120
The B.A. program provides students with the opportunity to pursue a career in criminal justice, social work, counseling, or psychology.
General Education Units: 51 · Major Units: 39 · Elective Units: 30 · Total Program Units: 120
The B.A. in Education (Pre-Professional track) equips students with the necessary skills, knowledge, and experiences to pursue professional careers or advanced study in the field of education.
General Education Units: 50 · Major Units: 61 · Elective Units: 9 · Total Program Units: 120
The B.A. in Bible and Theology degree equips students with a deep understanding of scripture and theological principles, preparing them for impactful ministries and careers.
General Education Units: 57 · Major Units: 48 · Elective Units: 15 · Total Program Units: 120
The B.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies program prepares you to think critically and solve problems by drawing from various fields, making you a more versatile professional.
General Education Units: 51 · Elective Units: 69 · Total Program Units: 120
The Master of Education in Educational Leadership instructs aspiring school administrators in scientific research, pedagogy, and instructional technology. Total Program Units: 30
The MBA program provides rigorous courses that develop your leadership skills and sharpen your business acumen. Total Program Units: 36

The Clinical Mental Health Counseling (CMHC) is a graduate-level program focused on effectively equipping students to earn licensure as a professional counselor (LPC). The CMHC program also prepares students for the successful pursuit of doctoral studies in Counseling. CACREP Accredited. Total Program Units: 60
This degree will prepare you with advanced leadership skills for ministry and traditional workplace environments. Total Program Units: 36

The Master of Divinity offers a thesis and non-thesis option as well as specializations in Biblical Languages, Biblical Studies, Chaplaincy, Counseling, Family Ministries, Intercultural Studies, Global Compassion Ministries, Islamic Studies, Practical Theology, and Theological Studies. Total Program Units: 72

The Master of Arts in Intercultural Studies degree program integrates theological, missiological, and practical training to equip graduates with skills and tools to impact diverse groups of people, especially in cross-cultural ministries. Total Program Units: 36
The Master's degree in Practical Theology prepares you in the areas of biblical studies, theological understanding, and practical ministry. Total Program Units: 36
The Master of Arts in Bible and Theology provides advanced knowledge in the study, interpretation, and application of the Word of God. Total Program Units: 36
The Master of Arts degree in English provides graduate students with advanced training in English and its specialized disciplines. Total Program Units: 30

The Master of Arts in Children & Family focuses on improving the lives of children, families, and communities, and is an excellent way for students to prepare for doctoral studies in Children and Family Studies. Total Program Units: 36

The Master of Arts in History is designed to deepen students' understanding of historical events, themes, and methodologies, providing a strong foundation for pursuing a Ph.D. and a variety of career paths. Total Program Units: 30

The Doctor of Ministry in Leadership (DMin) provides students the opportunity to gain advanced training in leadership, with special focus opportunities in communication and technology, cultural engagement, or general ministries.

The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) strengthens ties between academia and industry, fostering collaborations between the development of advanced research that synthesizes theoretical knowledge with cricual [sic], real-world business problems.

pages.title: Student Life – Catalyst Bible College
content: Starting in the Fall of 2025, each student will be asked to pay $2,000 a semester in student fees. This covers technology maintenance, administrative costs, partnership fees, student life activities, and practicum development. Those enrolled with Nelson University will have their student fees included in their bill from Nelson.
Student Chapel (section heading from saved copy)

All on-campus students will be asked to attend one chapel service a week and sign up for a small group in their respective ministry area (i.e. Young Adults or Adults). Chapel services will traditionally be held on Wednesdays and last 60 minutes. Services will be devotional in nature and have guest speakers.
Networking Opportunities (section heading from saved copy)

Students will be able to interact, network, and learn from prominent leaders across the country multiple times each semester. Students will also have the chance to engage with local community leaders during their time as students.
Community Life (section heading from saved copy)
Monthly, students will be able to participate in a community-building activity such as bowling, laser tag, a movie, or a "family dinner."
Leadership Labs and Crossfire (section heading from saved copy)

Each week, students will gain practical insights on future career preparation through Leadership Labs. In addition to Labs, students will participate in Crossfire discussion that challenge their worldview and encourages them to deep dive into the Bible.
Catalyst Bible College Student Housing is available to enrolled CBC Students. In order to qualify for student housing, you must:
Be an active, enrolled student with CBC
Apply through the Catalyst Offices prior to the start of the semester
Please note students who live an hour outside of campus receive priority placement in Student Housing

CBC has the ability to house full-time students, just minutes away from our Visalia campus. Students have a payment of $450/month including rent, utilities, and house furniture. Students will have one-two roommates when they live in CBC student housing. Students are not required to live in student housing while enrolled.
Contact the Catalyst Student Success Office for housing policies and payment information.

pages.title: Apply Here – Catalyst Bible College
content: Click Here to Start Your Application → https://connect.nelson.edu/apply/
When applying to Catalyst Bible College, you will create an application with Nelson University first.
Choose "Create an Account" under First Time Users.
Complete the form that asks for your Email Address, First Name, Last Name and Birthdate.
Next, you will receive a temporary PIN that will be sent to your email. From there, you will be asked to create a password for your Nelson application account.

Once your password is completed, you will select Start New Application. The application type you will choose will be: Main Application and Undergraduate Partner Site Admissions Application. If you are applying for a graduate program, you will select Graduate Admissions Application.
You will then be taken to your live application. Under the tab "Applicant Information", you will select Visalia, CA // Catalyst Bible College from the drop down menu.
Everything that remains on the application will be personal and academic history and information. If you need assistance in completing the application, please contact our CBC offices.

Once your application is completed, every student will be presented to the Catalyst Bible College staff for approval. It will noted [sic] in your application's outstanding items as "SOM Site Approval." The CBC staff will determine if you are an eligible candidate for enrolling and notify Nelson of the decision for acceptance.

pages.title: CA Disclosures – Catalyst Bible College
content: Click the button below to visit the Nelson University California Disclosures page.

Nelson University-Catalyst Bible College does not have dormitory facilities under its control. The university does not have a responsibility to secure housing for students. Catalyst Bible College has a current arrangement with a local apartment complex for students needing housing. Students pay $450/month, which includes rent, utilities, and furniture. Students have one or two roommates, depending on the size and location of the apartment. Should students prefer a different option, other local apartments are available, with rent prices ranging from $1,800 to $2,300/month, depending on the desired size and location.
